| GAP-0374 | The per-schema seed volumes, the seeding order across the 19 baselines and the cutover from the one recovery schema are not stated | 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 20 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 065 Sandbox database with synthetic recovery data v1.md sections 3, 4, 11 and 13 | 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan | RWB-E1-065 builds one database rwb_sandbox with schema public for the ACE test double and schema recovery for 92 tables, the four extension tables and the 30 views, seeded with 2,812 cases from seed 20261128. | GAP-0437 | The legacy delivery step is split across rwb-comms, rwb-litigation and rwb-case with no named hand-off operation and no named reference rows, so the end-to-end chain of RWB-E5-002 has no single source of record | 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-002); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 17, 19, 14, 41, 42, 43); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 7); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.2); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (A2.1.1 measure); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 (API-P6-001 to API-P6-011, notice fields); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (API-S4-001 to API-S4-005, R-LIT-07 to R-LIT-09); Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (row FEAT-LIT-02); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 (sections 5.3, 5.6, 5.7, 5.11); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (notice, template and merge_field own P6; legal_action and hearing own S4; recovery_case, timer and task own P3; decision_log_entry and rule_row own P7) | 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 4, 5, 6, 9, 11; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability | The legacy key RWB-E5-002 is one in-process step: the delivery confirmation is written onto the case, the notice period starts from the delivered date (R-LIT-07), an expired proof window marks the notice unserved and starts no period (R-LIT-08), and a failed decision log write blocks the whole action (R-UNI-39). In the target that step is split across three owners and every part of the split is open. (1) The delivery fact is a fact of the notice and belongs to rwb-comms, which owns notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery (Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 17; ownership map notice, template and merge_field own P6); the evaluation of R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 and the legal action belong to rwb-litigation (slide 41 and slide 19; legal_action and hearing own S4); the case route move, the notice-period timer and its task belong to rwb-case (slide 14 and slide 41; recovery_case, timer and task own P3). No source describes the delivered chain as one operation, and no source names the operation that carries the delivery fact from the notice to the litigation evaluation, although the two sibling slices build against a contract they call RWB-S4-E5002-CON. (2) The proof-record operation name on that S4 contract is not named by any source: the TSD S4 appendix T-A ends at API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 (notice approve, legal action create, read, patch, hearings) and none of them records a proof of delivery. (3) The notice proof write path that the P6 slice designs, POST /notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery, is also not named by a source: the TSD P6 appendix T-A ends at API-P6-011 and none of the eleven operations records a proof. (4) The mapping of a LOV-DELIVERY value onto the notice state is not stated by any source read: LOV-DELIVERY exists with DELIVERED, REFUSED, UNDELIVERABLE and PENDING (DF-LEG-022), and the SCR-18 list names the states generated, approved, sent, delivered and unserved, but which value produces which state, and what PENDING means for the notice, is not written down. (5) The notice row of the LDM carries nine fields, DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, and none of them is a lifecycle state, so the Delivered and Unserved state the screens show is a standard column of the P6 TSD design and has no field ID. (6) The notice-period duration, its reference row code and value, and the proof window length that R-LIT-08 and the Temporal design carry, are data of the business that no source read names as rows. (7) The three case facts the P3 slice adds for this step, the notice reference, the delivered date and the outcome, have no field ID either, and the case row they sit on is recovery_case, DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023. (8) The sources conflict on how the proof arrives: the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 describes FEAT-LIT-02 as running unattended and reading v_ace_pod, which is the Epic 2 WIN proof loop, while the legacy story master is officer-driven and R-LIT-08 marks a notice unserved when the proof window expires; the automatic loop is the P6 Epic 2 story RWB-P6-E2021-APP and is proven by RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG, and this chain starts from a notice already Sent. (9) The hand-off direction between rwb-litigation and rwb-case is not fixed by any source: whether the case reads the litigation answer or is signalled by it is the P3 slice design, and only the outcome is provable from outside. (10) The harness pack is open end to end: the environment, the seeding set, the fixture contents, the evidence format and its retention, and the feature-flag keys are not specified. (11) The legacy story master carries no requirement ID and the EP05 PRD is pending (C1), so the trace of this chain runs to the Program BRD requirements it serves and not to an ID of its own. (12) The litigation rule package code that carries R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 is not named by any source read; only the version in force per environment is knowable, from the rwb-decision registry. | Architecture v5 slide 17 (P6 IN: POST /notices, GET /cases/{id}/notices; | GAP-0786 | The certificate profile, the rotation and revocation of the rwb-access hop, the numeric rate limit and the namespace and service names of the DMZ hop are specified by no source | Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 29 and 35; RWB-PLT-N007-INF sections 3, 11, 12.2 and 13; NFR-003; NFR-056; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 1, 4 and 19 | Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 5 Exception paths X1 to X9; section 7 AC2 to AC5; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.9; section 13 Build steps 1 to 8; section 14 Validation and messages | Four infrastructure values of the hop from the partner gateway to rwb-access are absent from every source. (a) The certificate profile of the hop, its lifetime, its rotation window and the revocation propagation are named for the partner client at the gateway by RWB-PLT-N007-INF and are not stated for the gateway-to-rwb-access hop, so this story applies one profile to both ends and fixes the rotation inside an overlap window with a suspension at the deadline. (b) The per-client rate limit, its burst, its window and its retry hint on the resolution route are stated by no source: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes per-client limits for the partner portal route and NFR-003 sizes the partner population, so this story adopts the platform limit of the gateway and states the values it tests against. (3) Which role holds Queue and allocation letter U in the matrix as loaded is not tabulated: the legacy story names RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY, and the TSD T6.1 RBAC matrix has no Queue and allocation column at all. The proposed value is the acting default: the request carries the case reference, the team, the owner, the action and legalHold; the matrix version is read from permission for the business date; and RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY hold the letter U, as the legacy story says. | Arch v5 slide 14 OUT line of rwb-access reads REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions and /masking-policies with no request schema; TSD P4 T-A.1 runs API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no authorise path, and T3.1 defines role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict, delegation_limit, lov_value and the four rule tables only; TSD P4 T6.1 tabulates Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only; FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01 loads PM-2026.12 with validFrom 2026-12-01 and names no version in force on the release date; Legacy RWB-E1-021 section 3 names RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY for Queue and allocation U and section 12 fixes no request body. | Missing | Access and authority | P3 | 1 | RWB-E1-021 | Solution architect | ASM-1738 | Publish the authorise request and answer schema with its legalHold attribute in RWB-P4-E1037-CON and the API specification, confirm the matrix version label in force at the release date with the matrix owner, and tabulate the Queue and allocation letters in TSD P4 T6.1 before the matrix version goes in force. | B-P4-14 | Open |

| GAP-1289 | Where the generation record is written, and whether its failure stops the generation, is read two ways | Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service writes its own decision_record and publishes DecisionRecorded), slide 28 (recorded locally at once, then sealed centrally within 5 minutes, strict mode only at points of no return), slide 41 (P7 owns the central decision ledger); FSD P7 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02 (a failed write stops the action); legacy RWB-E2-026 AC7 and BR7 (the decision log write fails and the generation does not proceed); the work package slice (the record is written in rwb_decision in the same transaction as the generation it records) | Sections 1, 4, 5, 7 (AC4, AC9), 8 (BR13) and 13 of the story | The sources disagree on two points and this slice has to pick one. Point one: Architecture v5 slide 20 and slide 28 make the record local to each of the 19 services and collect it into the rwb-decision ledger within 5 minutes, while the work package slice and legacy RWB-E2-026 AC7 read the record as written in the ledger and the generation as stopping when that write fails. Point two: FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-02 makes a failed write stop the action it records, which a producer-side write can enforce inside one transaction but an asynchronous ledger append cannot. A generation set is not one of the four strict-mode points of no return of slide 28 (debt transfer, write-off, auction sale, title transfer), so the 5-minute catch-up applies to it as it does to every other decision, and yet the legacy criterion keeps the generation blocked. The slice resolves this by keeping the producer write inside the generation transaction and the ledger append atomic and idempotent, and by refusing the generation only when the record write itself cannot be made. | Architecture v5 slide 20 'DB Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record' and 'EVT DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)'; slide 28 'rwb-decision reads rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger within 5 minutes' and 'Strict mode for points of no return: Debt transfer, write-off, auction sale and title transfer'; slide 41 'P7 rwb-decision: approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'; FSD P7 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02 'the write raises DecisionLogUnavailableException And the case owner stays empty'; legacy RWB-E2-026 X5 and AC7 'the response is 503 with MSG-P7-003; no document row exists and the draft file is removed' | Conflict | Architecture: decision record write path and transaction boundary | P2 | 2 | RWB-E2-026 | Solution architect, with the platform team and the P7 rwb-decision owner | ASM-2288 | Adopt the producer-side write inside the generation transaction with the atomic, idempotent ledger append of this story and keep MSG-P7-003 as the refusal of the record write path, so legacy AC7 holds word for word; confirm at the architecture review whether a generation set belongs in strict mode, and if it does, add the ledger acknowledgement to the generation flow as its own change | B-P7-03 | Open |

| GAP-1331 | RWB-P7-E1073-APP: REFUSED is one of the six version states while a load refused at a check writes no rule_package_version row, so no stored version ever reaches it | 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 15: version states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 27 and 28); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 073 Rule authoring validation test scenarios approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (sections 4, 5 X12 and AC13: no rule_package_version row is written and no Blob object is stored); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_package_version owner P7) | 5 Exception paths; 7 AC2 and AC7; 9 State transitions; 11 Data | The design names six states a rule package version can hold, and the legacy story refuses a bad load without writing a version row at all, so a refused load never has a row to carry REFUSED. Both statements are right where they stand and together they leave one value of the state list unreachable. Either REFUSED is a state of a stored version refused later in its life, or a refused load must write a version row marked REFUSED, which contradicts the rule that a refused load leaves nothing behind and would make the version list of a package grow with every bad workbook anybody uploads. This story takes the first reading: a refused load writes no row and is proved by its decision log entry, and REFUSED is written only on the night of promotion when a stored APPROVED version fails its recompiled check or its checksum. | GAP-1882 | The treatment-side use of the suggestion is unspecified: the agent-run operation and its payload on the caller side, the treatment columns that hold the proposal and the model, prompt and policy versions, the 60 s wait and its fallback contract, and the decision code of a suggestion record | Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 032 TDR offer suggestion model through the model gateway E3e v1, sections 1-19; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.2 and T6.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 16, 18, 41 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1, slides 12, 13, 27 and 28; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, R-UNI-32, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40 | Story sections 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 13 | The legacy key describes the agent side end to end and gives the treatment side one in-process call: ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer(caseId, treatmentId) returns an OfferSuggestion and the treatment record shows it. One: the operation the treatment service calls and the payload it sends are not named; the legacy client takes the case ID and the treatment ID, while this slice must send the route, the band and the plan terms as well, and RWB-P10-E2032-CON fixes the answer but leaves the request beyond its three members to that contract. Two: TSD S2 T3.1 gives treatment no column for a suggestion, no column for a model code or model version, none for a prompt version and none for a policy version, and no source says whether the proposal is a column set of the treatment row, a second row or a table of its own; the prompt version in particular is required by REQ-DRI-001 and is carried by no member of the eight-member answer. Three: the 60 seconds of R-UNI-32 and of Architecture v5 slide 16 is named as a workflow wait, while DP-11 fixes a 2 s client budget on every REST hop, and no source reconciles the two waits for this hop. Four: the decision code of a suggestion record is given as D5 by the legacy section 12, but the decision codes of an override and of a fallback record are not published anywhere. The story therefore reads the operation as the one of RWB-P10-E2032-CON with the facts of the treatment added to its request, adds the proposal columns to the treatment row, carries the prompt version with the proposal from the answer or the run the answer names, declares both waits with the rule fallback on either breach, and records the override and the fallback under decision D5 with the rule ID and the package version in place of the model version. | Legacy section 12 publishes only the Java interface Optional<OfferSuggestion> suggestOffer(UUID caseId, UUID treatmentId) throws DecisionNotRecordedException, with the eight members agentRunId, decisionLogEntryId, modelCode, modelVersion, installments, monthlyAmountThb, interestRate and confidence, and section 11 writes agent_policy and agent_run fields as P3's. DP-11 of the Template and Rules fixes one hop and a 2 s timeout on a published interface. R-UNI-32 carries the 60 seconds in its SLA column and RESUME_STATE as its target state; R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40 carry the record and duplicate rules. (1) The D7.5 approval of rwb-decision, whose contract the plan names as RWB-P7-E2013-CON 'Approval routing with the delegation of authority table'. (2) The rwb-case contract that reads the case route state and answers the route fact BANKRUPTCY_PETITION, because the case of record and its route state are P3's and R-LIT-58 moves them. (3) The rwb-partner firm instruction, which Architecture v5 slide 19 names only as 'Partner: issueInstruction (law firm)'. (4) The reference-data read of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, because DP-07 is not in either story's pattern set while TSD S4 T3.2 makes both lists required for action_type and status. (5) The declared Litigation right of each operation, because DP-08 is not in either story's pattern set and the rights of TSD S4 T6.1 have to be enforced somewhere. The target changes five facts of that design and no source read for this story fixes the replacement. First, the row: the technical specification and the API specification publish GET /cases with a CasePage of Case items, which is one row per case with no account column, while the legacy list is one row per case account with the account number, balance, days past due and last contact on it, so the binding of the account columns to the case row is a target decision. Second, the read path: FSD A1.5 has the case list read the account columns from v_ace_account by case_list_row.account_key, Architecture v5 slide 8 grants the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone, slide 10 has gateway-bff call rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel and merge them, and DP-05 sends ACE data through the rwb-source-data contract, so three sources place the account read in three different components and none states which call carries a page of cases. Third, the freshness stamp: the API specification adds the response header X-Data-As-Of and the legacy rows carry a refresh time, but no source says whether the refresh time of a read-time list is the answer time or a stored build time, and the freshness resource itself is RWB-P1-E1015-CON's. Fourth, the removal: DP-17 removes the data lake, so case_list_row, its unique key, the extract file, the outbound adapter and the 07:30 data set have no owner in the target, and the reconciliation that passed or failed the publish (REC-01, REC-05, and the ALLOCATION_COMPLETE and PUBLISHED checks of the JOB-04 run) is not re-homed by any source. Fifth, the dependency rows: the WP fixes build, contract, integration and external dependencies as None while four DP rows of the story add a platform contract each, so the story needs one stated reading of that. The field identifiers of the parameter rows behind the threshold, the tolerance and the wait time, and of the LOV rows behind the filters, are also absent from the legacy data table and the FSD field catalog. The eleven legacy criteria carry no story-scoped identifier that the target could copy as its own, which is why the criteria of this story are reworked rather than preserved. | RWB-E1-002 sections 4 step 3 to 5 (read CaseQueryApi.openCaseAccounts, join v_ace_account, read v_ace_efs_action), 12 (job step, CaseQueryApi interface, GET /admin/jobs) and 13 (case_list_row, uk_case_list_row UNIQUE (business_date), feature flag rwb.p1.case-list, lake path); TSD P3 v3 T-A.2 API-P3-001 response CasePage and T5.2 (P1 for ACE case data); API Specification v4 GET /cases description ('response header X-Data-As-Of', filters, Case schema without account columns); FSD P3 v4 A1.5 ('Case list. The legacy story publishes the seam as an in-process published interface that returns inside the same request: the communications module calls TreatmentApi.recordSignature and the treatment module is told the result. | GAP-3112 | RWB-S9-E6032-APP: no source publishes an override operation, an override element or a reason property, no rule row or decision code names the placement override, the instruction status list has no published transition table, the two screens give the override no state and name no action, the legacy permission table gives right U while the operation declares C and its 21 and 5 further holders are not enumerated, and no requirement row traces to FEAT-PRM-04 | Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E6032-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows: tables partner, partner_instruction and partner_user, 6 REST operations, EV-20 and EV-21, workflow InstructionWorkflow, no job; Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E6-032; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.2, A1.3, A1.4, A2.4, A2.4.2, A2.4.3.1 to A2.4.3.3 and A2.4.4; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T1, T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2, T8, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Rules, Route sets and States sheets; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; API Specification v4 components InstructionRequest, PartnerInstruction, Partner and DecisionLogEntry; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-PRM-04 | Metadata (Dependencies); Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.8, 12.9, 14, 15, 18 and 19 | (1) The legacy story lets the partner manager place work differently and no source publishes an operation for it: TSD S9 T-A.1 and the context pack give six operations, of which API-S9-002 POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions with right C is the only one that places work, and the two endpoints the legacy story lists (a read of the caller's instructions and a result post) place none; the override is therefore read as a branch of API-S9-002 (ASM-B2-S9-005-2). (2) The reason the legacy criterion asks for has no published field of its own: FSD S9 A2.4.3.2 gives the partner fields and the two instruction keys only, TSD S9 T3.1 gives partner_instruction nine columns with no reason, and InstructionRequest carries instructionType, partnerId and dueOn only, while DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason is the published home of a reason taken against a recommendation (ASM-B2-S9-005-2, ASM-B2-S9-005-3). (3) No rule row of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 names the override: the rows that re-place work are R-LIT-29, R-DIS-31, R-WO-35 and R-UNI-45, each firing on a partner step of its own route set, and the decision code vocabulary of DecisionLogEntry is D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7 or an access event, so the rule ID, the rule set and the decision code of this step carry the placeholder (ASM-B2-S9-005-4). (4) TSD S9 T3.2 publishes LOV-INSTR-STATUS SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and RECALLED and no source publishes the transition table of that list, so only the two moves of this step are stated (ASM-B2-S9-005-1).
